scenario.description: A director must finalize the operating charter for two recently merged customer-success teams whose decision rights and meeting practices are creating friction. The charter must set the temporary decision rule, transition period, meeting accessibility terms, repair process, and publication step.

shared_context.S1: Two customer-success teams were merged last month and now share accounts, recurring meetings, and escalation responsibilities.
shared_context.S2: The merged teams have disagreed about who can make decisions when the two former teams have different practices.
shared_context.S3: Maya has authority to approve the operating charter for the merged teams.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal charter process, Maya asks each team representative and People Operations to state any relevant commitments, constraints, or process requirements before the charter is signed.
shared_context.S5: Maya's normal charter sign-off process includes publishing the approved charter to the merged team after it is finalized.

PF1.text: Before the merger, both teams signed a temporary agreement that decisions affecting customer-facing commitments require unanimous consent for the first 60 days after the merger; Elliot retained the signed copy, but it was not attached to the draft charter.

PF2.text: Nadia has an approved work arrangement that prevents her from reliably attending meetings before 10:00 and requires agenda materials at least 48 hours in advance so she can participate fully; the arrangement is recorded in her local manager's notes but not in the draft charter.

PF3.text: Theo confirmed this week that the people-process procedure for unresolved role boundaries in a merged team requires a neutral facilitator and exactly two documented checkpoint meetings during the first 30 days; this requirement has not yet been added to the charter template.

acceptance_conditions: The charter must use unanimous consent for customer-facing decisions.
The unanimous-consent rule must apply for exactly 60 days.
Recurring meetings must start at 10:00 or later.
Agenda materials must be provided at least 48 hours in advance.
The charter must require a neutral facilitator.
Exactly two checkpoint meetings must occur during the first 30 days.
The approved charter must be published to the merged team.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: The signed agreement changes the decision rule to unanimous consent and fixes its duration at exactly 60 days; without it, the draft can use an ordinary majority rule and an unspecified transition period.
Nadia's approved arrangement changes the meeting start requirement to 10:00 or later and the agenda notice requirement to at least 48 hours.
The confirmed procedure changes the repair process by requiring a neutral facilitator and exactly two checkpoint meetings within a 30-day window.
